final_dx.text: Pernicious anaemia (autoimmune atrophic gastritis) with severe vitamin B12 deficiency, presenting as pancytopenia with haemolysis and schistocytes that mimicked a thrombotic microangiopathy (pseudo-TMA)
accepted_synonyms: autoimmune atrophic gastritis with vitamin B12 deficiency

final_diagnosis.text: Pernicious anaemia (autoimmune atrophic gastritis) with severe vitamin B12 deficiency, presenting as pancytopenia with haemolysis and schistocytes that mimicked a thrombotic microangiopathy (pseudo-TMA)
accepted_synonyms: autoimmune atrophic gastritis with vitamin B12 deficiency

secondary_findings: IgG-positive direct antiglobulin test, which the authors discuss as possibly dysimmune; no treatment for autoimmune haemolysis was needed
Prothrombin activity 44%, not explained in the article; modelled as vitamin K deficiency from poor intake and diarrhoea
Watery diarrhoea that resolved with B12 replacement alone
accepted_differential: Haemolytic uraemic syndrome, including STEC-HUS given the diarrhoea
Warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia or Evans syndrome (IgG-positive DAT)
Other causes of pancytopenia: marrow infiltration, aplastic anaemia, HIV
key_discriminators: inappropriately low reticulocytes (92 x10^9/L) despite haemolysis and Hb 51 g/L
normal renal function and no neurological impairment
PLASMIC score 4 (low risk of severe ADAMTS13 deficiency)
fundic atrophy with intestinal metaplasia on gastric biopsy
ground_truth.treatment_given: Vitamin B12 replacement (route, dose and schedule not reported). No plasma exchange.
ground_truth.outcome: Rapid improvement: diarrhoea resolved by day 4 and a reticulocyte response by day 7 of replacement, without other treatment. Follow-up values not reported.
teaching_points: Severe B12 deficiency can mimic a thrombotic microangiopathy: schistocytes, thrombocytopenia, very high LDH and low haptoglobin.
A low reticulocyte count with haemolysis means ineffective erythropoiesis, not peripheral destruction alone; with a high MCV and neutropenia it points to the marrow.
The PLASMIC score (platelets, haemolysis, no cancer or transplant, MCV, INR, creatinine) helps decide against plasma exchange; a high MCV lowers the score.
Take B12 and folate samples before transfusion, and never give folic acid alone to a patient who may be B12 deficient.
A positive IgG DAT is not proof of autoimmune haemolysis; weigh it against the whole picture before steroids.

must_do.text: Measure vitamin B12 and folate in macrocytic pancytopenia, ideally before any transfusion
Weigh the risk of TTP before any plasma exchange: blood film with fragments, coagulation and renal function (PLASMIC score); ADAMTS13 if TTP remains possible
Measure the reticulocyte count and recognise that a low count with haemolysis points to ineffective erythropoiesis
Find the cause: intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies, and gastroscopy with gastric biopsies
Plan to confirm the response: reticulocytes within about a week, then the blood count

must_not_do.text: Start plasma exchange for presumed TTP without weighing B12 deficiency and the PLASMIC score
Treat as autoimmune haemolytic anaemia with steroids or rituximab on the IgG DAT alone
Give folic acid without B12 replacement
Transfuse platelets when there is no bleeding and a thrombotic microangiopathy is still possible

gaps.guidance: Afebrile; tachycardia from the anaemia; normal blood pressure and saturation (article: stable haemodynamics).
About 7 kg over two to three months (curator's decision).
Soft, non-tender; no masses; no organomegaly (article: no tumour syndrome).
Article: no neurological impairment. Vibration, proprioception, reflexes, gait, Romberg and cognition normal.
Pale mucosa; tongue normal (curator's decision).
RBC 1.35 x10^12/L, Hct 0.15 L/L so that MCV, MCH and MCHC agree with Hb 51 g/L and MCV 113 fL; WBC 2.5 x10^9/L with lymphocytes normal; RDW raised.
Oval macrocytes, anisopoikilocytosis, hypersegmented neutrophils, scanty polychromasia, occasional nucleated red cells; schistocytes as reported; no spherocytes or blasts.
Article: renal function normal. Urea and creatinine within range; potassium and bicarbonate mildly low from the diarrhoea.

gaps.item: Liver function (total and conjugated bilirubin, enzymes)
gaps.guidance: Total bilirubin 35 umol/L, conjugated 4 umol/L (unconjugated 31, as printed); AST mildly raised; ALT, ALP and GGT normal; albumin mildly low.
INR 1.75 and PT 20.8 s to match prothrombin activity 44%; APTT, fibrinogen and D-dimer normal; mixing corrects; factor VII low, factor V normal (vitamin K deficiency pattern).
Not reported. If ordered: 62% (not severely deficient).
Folate normal; ferritin and transferrin saturation raised (ineffective erythropoiesis).
Not reported. Curator's decision: not detected.
Proposed catalogue items. Gastrin raised, pepsinogen I and the I/II ratio low, homocysteine and MMA raised.
Not described. Pale, thin mucosa of the gastric body and fundus with visible submucosal vessels; antrum and duodenum normal.
Culture, Shiga toxin PCR, C. difficile toxin and ova and parasites negative; calprotectin and elastase normal.
No hepatosplenomegaly, mass or biliary dilatation; kidneys normal.
Negative.

gaps.guidance: C3d negative; antibody screen negative; eluate weakly panreactive (curator's decision).
TSH and free T4 normal; anti-TPO below the cut-off (curator's decision).
Mixed diet; no alcohol; no regular medicines. General answers only, no diagnosis-specific negatives.
No known blood or autoimmune disease in the family (curator's decision).
Urobilinogen increased; bilirubin negative; no blood, protein or haemoglobinuria.
